world.name: the shuttered bell foundry at Thistledown, dark since its founder stopped answering the door
world.scale: one evening, one foundry and its casting yard
physics_notes: the foundry keeps its own time in strikes and pulls, not clock hands
cast metal holds the day's warmth long after the fires go cold
the peal mechanism stores a pull and spends it as a swing, gently

cast.name: Founder Josiah Vane
cast.kind: the foundry's bell-founder, gone from Thistledown for decades

affordances.presence: moulds, tuning marks, and bells cast true
affordances.manner: exacting, dry-humored, careful of the metal

cipher_forms.text: peal changes: read each pull as long or short and let the repeating phrase spell out the setting

access_details.text: a spare foundry key hung on a nail behind the loose flue grate, exactly where the note's fold points
a catch hidden under the tuning board's lip trips the side door open if you know where to press
the last bell-ringer walks them in through the casting floor door, keys jingling on his belt

cipher_hint_carriers.text: a tuning hammer with the founder's own notes scratched along the handle, each mark keyed to a pull
a brass calibration scale bolted by the mould bench, its notches climbing by the same carry the peals use
a rack of tuning forks sorted low to high, each one labeled with a pull count
noon light through the belfry louvers falls across a marked floor plank, lining up with the peal's count

room_curiosities.text: Josiah Vane's own leather apron, still hanging by the casting floor, pockets worn to the shape of his tools
a small hand bell cast crooked on purpose, the founder's first failed attempt kept as a joke
a fingernail-sized model of the belfry frame, every bell set true in its place
sun through the coloured glass transom scatters bell-shaped light across the pattern room floor

vault_contents.text: the founding charter of Thistledown's bell, signed by the town and the founder both
a ledger of every wedding and homecoming the bell has rung for, kept faithfully for a century
Josiah Vane's own marking chisel, kept oiled as though he'd be back for it

obstacle_kinds.text: the bell-frame catwalk, planks slick with tallow, crossed one handhold at a time between the swinging cradles
the bell-frame catwalk clears only between strikes, so crossing means timing each dash to the swing

safeguards.text: a trip-wire strung to a hand bell rings the yard the moment a hand strays near the vault
the vault's counterweighted door swings shut on its own the instant it opens without the right sequence

remedies.text: a tuning key improvised from a bent nail walks a seized pin back to true
releasing the cradle's safety catch and easing it back to rest resets the jammed pull

loft_signatures.text: a half-finished mould still cooling on the bench, waiting for hands that never came back
every casting tool racked and labeled, ready for a workday that never resumed

motifs: the bell keeps the town's count
small true notes outlast big loud ones
prohibitions: never stand under a swinging cradle
never touch a mould before it has cooled
the frame moves only with the ringer's word
